newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine market-makers struggle to stay in club.
newsitem.headline: Argentine market-makers struggle to stay in club.

text.p: Argentina's Treasury bill market-makers, struggling to hang onto their place in the exclusive club, have fiercely undercut each other's bids at recent auctions, distorting the fledgling market.
"Market-makers are fighting to continue being market- makers," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.

Bankers and a government official told Reuters the latest auction yields were skewed by extremely low, cutthroat bids placed by market-makers and aspirants ahead of the March 31 review of who will be in the group for the next year.

The competitive thrashing allowed Argentina to allocate 500 million pesos this week in one-year Letes at a cut-off yield of 6.8 percent -- compared to analyst expectations of 7.2 percent to 8.5 percent.
"The factor (of aspiring) market-makers played an important role," said Esteban Thomsen, chief economist at ING Barings.

Market-makers need to ensure they take a certain volume at the monthly auctions -- one of the criteria of remaining in the 12-member club. And in the recent tournament to be a market-maker, rates are hitting bottom.

The mandate of the current market-makers runs out on March 31, when the Economy Ministry will evaluate whether to retain all the current members. The decision will be based on a snapshot of the institution's standing as a market-maker as of that day.
The ministry will rank the brokerages on criteria they have to meet during the year: volume traded in the market, amounts bought at the auctions, and other factors.

The new group of market makers will be announced on April 1, at which time the ministry will also make public the ranking of those in the group -- a ranking that has until now only been known by the ministry and the members.
Bankers told Reuters the main worry of current market-makers is the strong presence of Dutch bank ING Barings in the market -- which is aggressively seeking membership.
Even if the rewards of being in the system now are not huge, the future will bring more as the market develops, bankers said. Apart from that, the prestige of being a market-maker is indisputable.

The fierce competition has benefitted the Argentine government, which has been able to raise extremely cheap financing. But it has also distorted pricings in a system that the government is hoping to develop to issue more local debt.
"Primary market yields have come in much lower than secondary market yields," an analyst said.
What is more, the same system is also used for the issuance of Bonte Treasury bonds, which will be issued with increasing frequency in coming years.

"The evolution of the prices of these instruments (Letes and Bontes) will become a point of reference for use by the public and private sector," the Economy Ministry said last April when it announced the new system.
For that to be the case, it may be time to change the criteria for being a market-maker, some observers believe.

The current members are Banco Credito Argentino, Banco de Galicia y Buenos Aires, Banco Frances del Rio de la Plata, Banco Rio de la Plata, Banco Roberts, Banco Santander, BankAmerica Corp, Chase Manhattan Bank, Citicorp, Deutsche Bank, J.P. Morgan and Bank of Boston.
